note: Rewritten from Emerson 1956 (American Museum Novitates No. 1771), original in English. The species is described from the queen (morphotype queen) only, the type locality being near Nsakaru Hill, Nyasaland; the soldier and worker are not described and are placed under "Other" as the standard requires. In table 2 (measurements of the morphotype queen), apart from the head width of 1.81 mm, the OCR of the scan is defective and cannot be read line by line, so the remaining values are not recorded. Figure 5 (queen head and pronotum in dorsal view) has not been translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Named on the morphology of the queen: head and pronotum brownish black, the bases of the hairs and setae of the head, thorax and abdomen marked with pale dots; postclypeus with a median longitudinal black line; pronotum with a broad Y-shaped groove, the branches of the groove concolorous with the pronotum and the stem dark. Vertex with many long setae and numerous short hairs, but without a distinct hair pad. Closest to A. trägårdhi, more distant from A. arquieri (the latter with a shinier head surface and a wider head and postclypeus).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Queen (morphotype, fig. 5): head and pronotum brownish black, the bases of the setae and hairs of the head, thorax and abdomen marked with pale dots; postclypeus with a median longitudinal dark line. Pronotum with a broad Y-shaped groove, the branches concolorous with the pronotum and the stem dark. Abdominal tergites brown; sternites brown with a white spot anteriorly. Vertex with many long setae and numerous short hairs, but without a distinct hair pad. Pronotum and wing pads with many long setae and short hairs. Tergites and sternites with medium-length setae at the sides and scattered short setae and hairs in the middle, these hairs extending backwards over the white part of the posterior margin of each tergite. The white membrane on the ventral side of the queen's abdomen bears numerous short hairs. Head broadly oval, slightly wrinkled above, with irregular facets and muscle attachment scars anteriorly. Fontanelle white, larger than the ocellus and smaller than the pale antennal base. Compound eyes relatively small. The upper margin of the ocellus is a raised projecting edge of the head capsule, and there is a small narrow white band on the head capsule below the ocellus; the distance between the ocellus and the eye suture is slightly greater than the length of the ocellus itself, and the surface of the ocellus is nearly vertical. Postclypeus slightly more than half as long as wide. Antennae broken (15 segments visible intact), segment 3 distinctly shorter than segment 4, segment 4 distinctly shorter than segment 2. Mandibles, as seen without dissection, similar to those of the A. angustatus worker figured by Ahmad (1950, p. 69). Pronotum about half as long as wide, slightly narrower than the head; anterior margin without a notch, posterior margin shallowly notched and weakly lobed. Posterior margins of the meso- and metanotal tergites broadly concave, the angles about 140—150 degrees, the posterior lobes rounded and slightly wrinkled behind. Fore coxa with a sharp longitudinal ridge whose projecting peak forms a peak angle of about 135 degrees in lateral view. Basal three tarsal segments with dark, broadly rounded projections. Measurements in table 2 (mm): head width 1.81 (the other lines of the table are defective in the OCR and are not recorded).
